questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mongolia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mongolia article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city is Ulaanbaatar.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mongolia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mongolia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mongolia article.

questions.proof: It has a border with Russia to the north and the People's Republic of China to the south and southeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mongolia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Mongolia article.

questions.proof: The official language of Mongolia is Mongolian.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Most of Mongolia's foreign relations are with _____ and China.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “China”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Foreign relations” part of the Mongolia article.

questions.proof: Most of Mongolia's foreign relations are with Russia and China.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Mongolia joined the World Trade Organization in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mongolia article.

questions.proof: Mongolia joined the World Trade Organization in 1997.
